A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Render-in-the-Loop work. All 25 pages of v1 and 29 pages of v3, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, support comparison. Relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original Text-to-SVG and Image-to-SVG experiments, component ablations, and generated examples in Section 4, Tables 1–2, and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds inference-cost measurements, threshold-sensitivity results, and failure examples in Table 3, Table S1, and Figure 5.

M1.justification: VSF training, path decomposition, the loss, and RaV verification/resampling procedures remain unchanged. v3 clarifies the rationale for forced termination and acknowledges the additive action space; it does not introduce a different stopping procedure or editing operations.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 0.85M MMSVG training subset and 600-sample MMSVGBench covering text/image-conditioned icon and illustration generation. The new diagnostic analyses and failure examples do not establish additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparators. For Table 2, v1 assigns Qwen3-VL to Text-to-SVG and GPT-5 to Image-to-SVG, whereas v3 says both backbones were evaluated on both tasks. The table retains identical values without separate backbone rows, so the claimed expansion of comparator participation cannot be verified.

E3.justification: v3 adds a controlled latency/token comparison using the same Qwen3-VL backbone, vLLM stack, and V100 hardware, plus loose/default/strict RaV threshold settings on MMSVG-Illustration Text-to-SVG. It also revises the stated backbone-to-task assignment for Table 2, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Existing training settings and benchmark metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands diagnostics beyond the retained component ablations: Section 3.4 analyzes inference overhead, Appendix A.1 tests RaV threshold sensitivity, and Section 3.5 examines repetition, unusual semantic states, and compositional omissions. The instruction-following examples and gallery are relocated existing evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests for its experiments. The new threshold study also reports point estimates only.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their numerical results. New Table 3 reports 28.77 versus 43.19 seconds for open-loop SFT versus VSF, with 550.94 versus 804.31 tokens and 0.038 seconds of rendering. Table S1 adds threshold-dependent scores, and Figure 5 adds three failure outcomes. These are additional findings, not improved benchmark scores over v1.

T1.justification: The sequence formulation, masked autoregressive objective, and appendix rendering/difference equations are unchanged. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs; the revised stopping explanation is an interpretation rather than a new formal assumption or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and principal conclusion retain the same claims about visual feedback, VSF/RaV, competitive SVG generation, and data efficiency. The additional diagnostics support or qualify these claims without redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: v1 treats repeated verification failures as evidence of completion and describes overhead as slight. v3 explains forced stopping as protection against a stalled or incapable policy, quantifies 1.50× latency, and acknowledges that accepted primitives cannot be undone or replaced. It adds semantic/compositional failure boundaries and attributes overhead mainly to decoding. However, Appendix B retains the older completion assumption.

D1.justification: v3 documents vLLM and V100 hardware for the new timing experiment and specifies the additional threshold pairs in Table S1. Existing training hyperparameters, CairoSVG renderer, system prompts, and trajectory examples are retained; no new code or data access provision is supplied.

R1.justification: Appendix F substantially broadens research positioning with a new subsection linking SVG generation to layout, 3D synthesis, motion/geometry models, agents, and human-centered applications. Nineteen works are added and four removed, including Im2vec, StrokeNuwa, and SVGFusion. VSF/RL complementarity is explained more explicitly; the renamed Reason-SVG reference remains the same work.

P1.justification: v3 reorganizes the main-text/appendix narrative: Related Works moves from Section 2 to Appendix F, references precede the appendices, and qualitative galleries move into an additional-analyses appendix. Setup and comparison prose are condensed, and stopping and naive-prompting explanations are rewritten. Affiliations are corrected and acknowledgements added.

P2.justification: v3 adds the inference-cost table, threshold-sensitivity table, and failure-case panel. v1 Figures 4–5 become appendix Figures S1–S2, and Figure 6 becomes Figure 4. Existing visual examples are retained, with localized caption, spacing, and placement changes rather than wholesale redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency through measured inference overhead, threshold-sensitivity evidence, concrete failures, and an explicit inability to revise accepted primitives. These make the unchanged method and benchmark results easier to assess critically. The gain is limited by the unresolved backbone attribution in Table 2 and inconsistent main-text versus appendix explanations of forced stopping.
